source_text: Let's write it the project steps for codex-33 as an E-aif-cascade.md note so that we can pass it an excursion not just a one-by-one list of tasks that can get forgotten and disrupt your workflow as well.  Regarding the reward for the bag, that's a bit unfortunate but maybe we should continue to elaborate the outer loop cascade and see if more requirements change the picture.  So, for example, I've mentioned "centrality" (akin to the work that claude-4 is doing on Lean4 rows, picking the terms that unblock the most rows and prioritising those) as well as "feasibility" (missions or excursions that require a large degree of operator HITs are not good candidates for overnight automation).  If these requirements are not in the outer loop cascade yet, we could complexify it.  It gets to a point where, in my view, it's not even possible to conceive of it as other than a cascade!

㊥ (gist) Written: `futon2/holes/E-aif-cascade.md` (futon2 `987898239`), the excursion that codex-33 works through item by item instead of waiting on packets from me. It records what is done today, then three sections of work with an acceptance bar per item: A, the R-nodes as a cascade (discovery → your ruling on the cut → Lean receipt → drawing → each R-unit read as a blend square); B, elaborating the outer-loop diamond with the two requirements you named; C, the causal reading and a chain comparison that is actually between constructible things. codex-33's A1 job has just finished; its wake has not reached me yet, so I will review it in the next turn.

㊢ ("centrality" and "feasibility" — where they stand) Centrality is already in the loop twice, in different forms: it is the live selector's *only* scored channel (`1/(1+occurrence count)` on the Cascade Live map — that is what chose `M-interim-director-proxy-metric-inventory`), and it is in the diamond's outcome vocabulary as `downstream-unblocking`. Feasibility is there once each side: the live selector's `:automated-feasibility` support filter, and the diamond's machine-side `injury` arm. **Operator-turn load is in neither.** So B1/B2 are discoveries of the two tokens (what "unblocks the most" means per task kind, citing claude-4's rows measure rather than recomputing it; the share of an item's recent touches that were operator turns), B3 pastes the two squares into the diamond as the blend reading requires — centrality consumed by the generative model's `downstream-unblocking` term, operator load either as a support change like `injury` or as a preference term, both written up for you to choose — as an edn diff and a receipt, and B4 measures whether the extension changes the ranking of the real run against the live selector's, under `E-outer-loop-improvement`'s ablation rule.

㊟ ("the reward for the bag, that's a bit unfortunate") Less so than it looks: the bag is not an arrangement the tokens admit — `fill` fires before the observation exists — so a constructed cascade never offers it, and the scorer only produced the number because it was handed the edge list. What the measurement does show is that a per-step C with no consumption rule would reward it if it were offered, which is C3's item: charge the token emitted with no consuming want. And yes — each requirement added is one more square with its own token, and the picture stops being describable as anything but a cascade; B3's receipt will make that literal (meets, linear extensions) rather than a claim.

㊭ (how the excursion runs) codex-33 takes the next unchecked item in its section; every item ends in a commit and a bell with the sha; I review (record, test adequacy, selective re-execution) before the next starts; your rulings — A2 the cut, B3 support-change vs preference, B5 promotion of `meta/select-the-meta-item`, and the two v3 decisions — are recorded in the note when given. Sections A and B can run on two seats if you want a second one minted; C1 waits for claude-17's page.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (gist) Yes — and the data already says what the simplification is. The harness figure is drawn from `p4ng/empirics-futon/aif-lean-dag.edn`: 17 drawn nodes, 43 edges, each edge a named Lean term (`o`, `mu`, `G`, `pi`, `C-tau`, `A`, `B`, …) with a class (23 imported, 10 absent, 6 present-not-imported, 1 unplaced). Those edges are already "what each step needs", carrying a token — the cascade's descent edge. What the wiring diagram has that a cascade cannot is a *cycle*: eleven of the seventeen nodes (R1 R2 R3 R3a R4 R5 R6 R7 R8 R16 R17) form one strongly connected component. So the cascade version is the wiring diagram cut at the tick: the edges that carry state into the *next* click become the click's initial haves, and what remains is one click's formation, acyclic, with its meets.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: (what the cut exposes) I tried the obvious cut inline — the enactment edges `R16→R1/R2` (`u`, `world`), the belief recurrence `R3→R1` (`s-next`), the learned parameters `R4→{R1,R2,R3,R3a}` (`A`,`B`), and the fit/precision feedbacks. Two small cycles remain: `R6⇄R17` (`pi` out, `E` back) and `R4⇄R7` (`A` out, `rates` back). Both are the same thing: one box holding two units. R6 is both *candidate action space* (produces π) and *selection* (needs G); R4 is both *forward model* and *the model whose parameters precision-estimation reads*. The figure can draw that as one box with arrows in and out; a cascade cannot, and splitting them is the simplification doing its work rather than a defect. With the eleven cuts in place, the remaining order already has 36 meets, among them `R19 ⊓ CTAU-TOKEN = R5`, `R1 ⊓ R19 = R5`, `R2 ⊓ R13 = R4`, `R13 ⊓ R14 = R6`: R5 is the meet of preference and prediction — G is the emergent structure of that square, which is your diamond-is-a-pattern point on the R-nodes themselves.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-2
previous_reply_acts.text: ("a simplification of the elaborated wiring diagram") What goes, and where it goes: the five stage columns become a receipt field (they are one coarse *parse* — perceive, believe, evaluate, select, act is the recipe, not the formation); the Lean modules per node and the consumer binders become the unit's `:source`; the edge class is kept, because it matters: an `:absent` edge is drawn precedence with no term carried in Lean, which in `ConstructionReceipt` terms is an edge whose token set is empty — `valid` would reject it exactly as it rejects the forged chain edge. Ten of the forty-three are in that class (all seven `R4→…` edges among them). So the cascade version of the figure would show, as a property of the order, which of the drawn dependencies the Lean model actually carries.

previous_reply_acts.text: (project, as checks) 1. A script beside `harness-figure.bb`, reading the same three p4ng files, that writes `r-cascade.edn`: units with modules, descent edges with token sets and class, the cut (each cut edge named with the reason: cross-tick state / learned parameter / split unit), the meets, the linear-extension count, and the `ConstructionReceipt` projection with absent-class edges flagged. 2. A drawing of it as a Hasse diagram or S-expression, not columns. 3. The Lean receipt for the result, as for the outer diamond. 4. Later, the comparison with the catalogue's Pattern map and the apparatus flexiargs, so each R-unit's IF/HOWEVER/THEN is read against its in- and out-tokens.

I will propose a cut in the discovery report with each cut edge justified from the term it carries, and you rule on it there rather than in the abstract.
